sharpe.label: Sharpe ratio
sharpe.def: Return earned above the T-bill rate for each unit of volatility (ups and downs). Higher is better; 0.5 is decent, 1.0 is strong.

information_ratio.label: Information ratio
information_ratio.def: How much a holding beat its benchmark per unit of the risk it took by differing from it (active return divided by tracking error). Above 0.5 is good, but it needs a t-statistic above about 2 to be believable.

max_drawdown.label: Max drawdown
max_drawdown.def: The worst peak-to-trough fall in month-end value. A -25% drawdown turns $100 into $75 before it recovers.

deflated_sharpe.label: Deflated Sharpe
deflated_sharpe.def: The probability that the Sharpe ratio is real after allowing for how many candidates were tried. Test dozens of names and the best one looks good by luck; 0.95 or more is convincing, below 0.5 is a coin flip.

out_of_sample.label: Out-of-sample (OOS)
out_of_sample.def: Data the selection never saw. Here: Jan 2018 to Oct 2026, with every screen built only from data up to Dec 2017.

in_sample.label: In-sample (IS)
in_sample.def: The 2010-2017 data that every screen and shortlist was built from. Good in-sample numbers say little about the future, so they sit beside the out-of-sample ones to show how much held up.

tracking_error.label: Tracking error
tracking_error.def: How much a holding's returns differ from its benchmark's, as an annual standard deviation. Low means it behaves like the benchmark.

t_stat.label: t-statistic
t_stat.def: How many standard errors an average is away from zero. Above about 2 the result is unlikely to be luck; below 1 it is indistinguishable from noise.

non_us_share.label: Non-US share
non_us_share.def: The part of the portfolio value that counts as non-US under the course rule (foreign-domiciled companies and EM bond issuers count fully; gold, silver and US stocks count zero). The client needs at least 70%.

cagr.label: CAGR
cagr.def: Compound annual growth rate: the steady yearly return that would produce the same end value.

volatility.label: Volatility
volatility.def: Annualised standard deviation of monthly returns: the typical size of the swings.

beta.label: Beta
beta.def: How strongly the holding moves with its benchmark: 1.0 moves one-for-one, 2.0 doubles the swings.

alpha.label: Alpha
alpha.def: Annual return left after accounting for beta, i.e. what the holding added beyond its benchmark's movement.

sortino.label: Sortino ratio
sortino.def: Like the Sharpe ratio but only downside swings count as risk.

calmar.label: Calmar ratio
calmar.def: Annual return divided by the size of the worst drawdown.

up_capture.label: Up / down capture
up_capture.def: How much of the benchmark's gains (up) and losses (down) the holding took part in. Up above 1 with down below 1 is the ideal.

rolling.label: Rolling 36-month
rolling.def: A measure recalculated every month over the latest 36 months. It shows whether an edge is steady or came from one stretch.

monte_carlo.label: Monte Carlo fan
monte_carlo.def: Thousands of simulated 7-year paths built by resampling real months of history. The band covers the 5th to 95th percentile of outcomes and the middle line is the median.

frontier.label: Efficient frontier
frontier.def: For each level of risk, the highest expected return a mix of the positions can deliver. Portfolios below the curve take risk without being paid for it.

tangency.label: Tangency portfolio
tangency.def: The mix on the frontier with the highest Sharpe ratio.

min_variance.label: Minimum-variance portfolio
min_variance.def: The mix on the frontier with the lowest volatility.

ex_ante.label: Ex-ante / ex-post
ex_ante.def: Ex-ante uses forward-looking expected returns; ex-post uses what actually happened in history.

fx_vol_share.label: FX share of variance
fx_vol_share.def: How much of a foreign holding's dollar volatility comes from currency moves rather than the asset itself.

hedge_cost.label: Hedge cost
hedge_cost.def: What it costs per year to remove currency risk with forward contracts: the interest-rate gap between the two currencies plus fees.

local_vs_usd.label: Local vs USD return
local_vs_usd.def: Return in the asset's home currency compared with the dollar return the US investor gets. The difference is the currency effect.

consensus.label: Expected 7-year return
consensus.def: The middle of at least two forward models (CAPM, discounted cash flow, Grinold-Kroner, yield). An estimate with a wide range, not a forecast.

stress.label: Stress test
stress.def: The total return over a past crisis window; for the portfolio, what today's holdings would have lost.

rubric.label: Rubric score
rubric.def: The pre-registered 100-point score that ranks candidates within a type (out-of-sample Sharpe, information ratio, drawdown, forward return and others). Fixed before any backtest.

drop_rule.label: Drop rule 8.2
drop_rule.def: A candidate is dropped when its out-of-sample Sharpe is below its type's benchmark and its information ratio is below zero.

rf.label: Risk-free rate
rf.def: The return on 1-3 month Treasury bills (BIL). Sharpe ratios subtract it.

turnover.label: Turnover and cost drag
turnover.def: How much of the portfolio is traded at each rebalance and the yearly return lost to trading costs.

sleeve_mix.label: Sleeve mix
sleeve_mix.def: The split between stocks, bonds and the 'other' sleeve (gold, silver). The brief asks for about 55 / 35 / 10 within a tolerance.

price_index.label: Price index
price_index.def: An index that ignores dividends. The home-market indices used for the local-currency view are price indices, which understates the benchmark's return.

growth_100k.label: Growth of $100k
growth_100k.def: What $100,000 invested at the start would be worth each month, after the modelled trading costs.

weights.label: Weight
weights.def: The share of the $100,000 put in one position.
